extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and researchers in philosophy of mathematics and mathematical practice (including mathematicians interested in epistemic/virtue-based evaluation of proofs, definitions, and concepts)
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and apply epistemic/virtue-based criteria for assessing mathematical definitions, concepts, proofs, understanding, and style as discussed in the philosophy of mathematical practice literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistemic virtues (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Epistemic virtues as a class of standards and values used to evaluate mathematical practice (including proofs, definitions, concepts, and methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry frames numerous topics under the heading of epistemic virtues and connects them to specific virtues such as naturalness, fruitfulness, transferability, fitness, and motivation; the literature includes virtue-theoretic treatments of mathematical practice (e.g., Aberdein et al. 2021; Tanswell & Kidd 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness and fruitfulness (of definitions and concepts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Naturalness and fruitfulness as pertains to definitions and concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as evaluative criteria for judging whether a definition or conceptualization is well-chosen for mathematical practice; discussed in the literature (e.g., Heuer, Pérez-Escobar and Sarikaya 2025; Morris 2024; Tappenden 2005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability, fitness, and motivation (as properties of proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transferability, fitness, and motivation as a property of proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualities are treated as criteria for assessing proofs—how well a proof transfers to related contexts, how 'fit' it is to the mathematical aims, and how well it is motivated; references include Easwaran 2009; Morris 2024; Raman-Sundström 2016; Raman-Sundström and Öhman 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical understanding as an evaluative aim/criterion for proofs and explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of proofs and explanations includes whether they promote understanding; extensive literature treats varieties and conditions of mathematical understanding (e.g., Avigad 2008, 2010, 2022; D’Alessandro 2023; Folina 2018; Macbeth 2012; Manders 2012; Hamami and Morris 2024; Tappenden 2005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical style
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical style considered as a criterion influencing presentation and evaluation of proofs and mathematical work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style (including choices of notation, visualization, exposition) is treated as relevant to how mathematics is practiced and assessed; see the entry on mathematical style and related literature (e.g., Mancosu 2021; Tanswell & Inglis 2024).
